record.context_brief: Mutually unbiased bases in composite dimensions
record.original_question: For a D-dimensional Hilbert space, determine the maximum number K of orthonormal bases that are mutually unbiased, meaning that every vector from one basis has squared inner-product magnitude 1/D with every vector from another basis. It is known that K = D + 1 can be achieved when D is a prime power; decide what happens for other composite dimensions, in particular whether seven mutually unbiased bases exist in dimension six.

evidence.quote: Determine the maximal number K of orthonormal bases in a D-dimensional Hilbert space, which are mutually unbiased in the following sense: If eki denotes the ith vector of the kth basis, all scalar products heki, enj i with k 6= n have the same absolute value (namely D−1/2).

It is known that if D is the power of a prime, K = D+ 1 can be reached, but this is not known for any other composite number. So the problem is already to decide whether there exist K = 7 mutually unbiased bases in D = 6 dimensions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a complex Hilbert space of finite dimension $D \geq 2$. Two orthonormal bases $\{e^{(k)}_i\}_{i=1}^D$ and $\{e^{(n)}_j\}_{j=1}^D$ of $\mathcal{H}$ are called mutually unbiased if 
$$|\langle e^{(k)}_i, e^{(n)}_j\rangle|^2 = \frac{1}{D} \quad \text{for all } i,j \in \{1,\dots,D\}.$$
A family of $K$ orthonormal bases is called a set of mutually unbiased bases (MUBs) if every two distinct bases in the family are mutually unbiased. Let $N(D)$ denote the maximum cardinality of such a family in dimension $D$. It is known that $N(D) \leq D+1$ for every $D$, and that $N(D) = D+1$ whenever $D$ is a prime power.

(a) Determine $N(D)$ for composite dimensions $D$ that are not prime powers.

(b) In particular, decide whether $N(6) = 7$; that is, determine whether there exist seven mutually unbiased bases in $\mathbb{C}^6$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem remains open. Dimension 6 is still the smallest dimension where the maximum number of MUBs is unknown; only 3 MUBs in C^6 have ever been constructed, and the conjecture that N(6)=3 (in particular that 7 MUBs do not exist) is unresolved. Recent work (2024–2025) reformulates the question as a polynomial optimization problem but has not settled it, and a 2025 comment identified errors in earlier partial proofs concerning Hadamard matrices in dimension 6.

status_evidence.claim: The MUB problem is still open in dimension 6.

status_evidence.claim: No set of 4 MUBs in dimension 6 has been found; conjectured maximum is 3.
